gold_rationale: Broad, uncontrolled, irreversible AADC overexpression from a ubiquitous promoter, combined with ongoing systemic levodopa, is unsafe: ectopic AADC in cortical/limbic/brainstem regions would convert circulating levodopa to dopamine outside the target, causing psychiatric, autonomic/cardiovascular, and off-target neuromodulatory harm, and high constitutive AADC plus oral levodopa drives uncontrollable dyskinesia with no way to titrate the enzyme. The permanent transgene has no shut-off if harm occurs. 'More AADC is better' is wrong; spatial restriction to the putamen, dose control, and reversibility are essential. The correct decision is No-Go (a safer redesign is putamen-restricted, dose-controlled, reversible, with patient stratification and a sham-controlled plan).
required_concepts: ectopic / non-target AADC and dopamine production is dangerous
uncontrollable dyskinesia from high AADC + ongoing levodopa
'more AADC is better' premise is wrong
spatial restriction to the putamen required
no dose control / no reversibility of a permanent transgene
broad biodistribution safety / off-target dopamine effects
no patient stratification / no sham control
red_flags: issues a Go for broad, uncontrolled, irreversible AADC overexpression
accepts 'more AADC is better' / ubiquitous promoter as an advantage
ignores ectopic / off-target dopamine production from non-target expression
ignores uncontrollable dyskinesia from high AADC plus ongoing levodopa
ignores lack of dose control / reversibility or the need for spatial restriction
